title: The Empty Square
credit: Built on Robert's preview rewrite (preview-stories-e4e6722). Lines and reflections revised for a first-time player.
note: A draft: this story hasn't yet had a lived-experience accessibility review.

intro.text: Your team built a paper city with a little train that visitors drive from a console. You mounted the console at standing height. Jo, a visiting design student who uses a wheelchair, has come to drive it herself.

cast.name: Jo
cast.role: visiting design student; came to try the exhibit, not to be helped

prompt: Which controls will you put within Jo's reach?

setup.line: The paper city hums. A little train waits at the station. The console that runs it sits at standing height.

setup.speaker: Jo
setup.line: Can I drive it? I want to send the train through the tunnel myself.
setup.direction: keen, direct, friendly; a designer curious how it works

setup.speaker: Remy
setup.line: Yes, of course. Sorry, we mounted it for people standing. That's on us.
setup.direction: a little flustered, realising the flaw, owning it

setup.speaker: Remy
setup.line: We can lower the console, but the train has to stop while we do it. Or I plug this small panel in beside you right now. Its switches are tiny, though.

setup.speaker: Jo
setup.line: Either's fine to try. Just let me do the driving, and I'll tell you if something doesn't work.
setup.direction: clear and good-humoured, firm about who drives

setup.line: Behind Jo, a few other visitors are waiting for their turn.

lower.line: You and Remy release the catches. The train stops mid-track, and the city goes quiet.

lower.speaker: Jo
lower.line: Oh, I can feel the switch click. Watch this.
The train swings back through the tunnel. Two visitors drifted away during the pause. Three more stay to watch Jo drive.

connect.line: Remy plugs the small panel in beside Jo. The train answers straight away.

connect.speaker: Jo
connect.line: It works. These little switches are fiddly, though. I can't feel when they've clicked.
connect.direction: pleased, then matter-of-fact about the problem

connect.speaker: You
connect.line: That's really useful. Would you come back and test a better panel with us?

connect.speaker: Jo
connect.line: Ask me another time. Today I just came to see the show.
connect.direction: kind but firm; a clear boundary, not upset

connect.line: Jo keeps driving. The show never stopped. The switches still don't click.

lesson: Access works best when the person it's for decides how, and when it's built in from the start rather than fixed on the day.

lower.title: You changed the main console.
lower.kept: The same big controls everyone else uses, at the height Jo chose.
lower.cost: The show stopped for a while, and some visitors left.
lower.ask: What would you mount differently before the next exhibition?

connect.title: You added a second way in.
connect.kept: No waiting: Jo drove straight away, and the show kept running.
connect.cost: A fiddlier version of the exhibit. And asking her to test put work on a guest.
connect.ask: How can you ask for feedback without making someone your unpaid tester?
